analysis: The supplied units are only CHANGELOG.md head text, a documentation-only change (mode 100644 unchanged). No executable code is visible, so no security regression can be shown from these units. The new entry, 'Unreleased — coordinator schema migrations', describes moving the Postgres schema to numbered goose migrations, with a 3s lock timeout, up to three attempts, an advisory lock, and a fail-startup-without-baseline behavior. That entry touches A-009 (payment ledger), A-015/A-016/A-017 (App Attest and qualification stores), and the legacy MDM cohort and revocation tombstone schemas. The Go migration code is not supplied. A next review pass should check these in the actual source: (1) that revocation tombstones and legacy cohort tables, and the frozen-cohort marker, are preserved exactly by the baseline migration; (2) that a failed or partial migration cannot start the coordinator with missing security-relevant columns or constraints, which would fail open for authorization or revocation (T-053, T-054); (3) that the advisory-lock and retry logic cannot be raced into a double-applied or skipped migration. The changelog also mentions the Stripe refund clock-skew fix (the exact-debit check is retained, relevant to T-030) and removal of the unauthenticated provider earnings endpoint (T-031), which the changelog says is now closed. The changelog claims in other entries, such as no provider identities exposed, macOS 27 reward gating, and fail-closed attestation challenges, align with the existing threat model (TB-009, TB-011) but are not verified here. No threat-model update gap is evident from the text alone. Coverage is limited to the changelog; needs_deeper_review is true because the migration source is not provided.
